words.meaning: A main section of a book or textbook.
System where power is shared between central and state governments.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author introduces this to define the core system of government where power is shared between the center and the states.
hard.simple_explanation: A system of government where power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a giant pizza where the Central Government decides the crust, but each State gets to pick its own toppings. That’s Federalism!

examples.text: Federalism in India ensures that both the Union and State governments have their own powers.
Because of federalism, my state has its own holidays, but the central government still decides when the big national festivals are!

hard.real_world_analogy: A school system where the Principal makes general rules for everyone, but each Teacher makes specific rules for their own classroom.

words.meaning: Something that happened or existed before now.

medium.simple_explanation: Something that happened or existed before the current time or event.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the 'Previously on...' recap at the start of a TV show that reminds you why the main character is currently screaming.

examples.text: In the previous chapter, we learned about the basics of government.
My previous attempt at baking a cake resulted in a rock that could break a window.

words.meaning: To have noticed or mentioned something specifically.
An arrangement of levels from top to bottom.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe the 'top-to-bottom' hierarchy of power distribution in a federal structure.
hard.simple_explanation: An arrangement that goes straight up or down rather than side to side.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of a tall stack of pancakes. The top one is the central government, and the ones below are the states. It's a tower of power!

examples.text: The vertical division of power moves from the Union government down to the Local bodies.
I tried to sleep in a vertical position like a bat, but I just ended up with a very sore neck!

hard.real_world_analogy: A ladder where the highest rung is the Central government and the lowest rung is the Village Panchayat.

words.meaning: The act of splitting something into separate parts.

medium.simple_explanation: The act of splitting something into separate parts or groups.
medium.funny_explanation: What happens to a giant pepperoni pizza when four hungry teenagers enter the room.

examples.text: The division of power between the state and the central government is key to federalism.
The division of chores in our house usually means I do everything while my brother naps.

words.meaning: The official right to make decisions and control.
Being in the middle of or included in a group.
Not the same as another thing.
Different layers or steps in a system.
Something that is very important or big.
Different types or kinds of something.
Using or having something together with others.
Relating to the present or recent times.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to the present time or using the newest ideas and technology.
medium.funny_explanation: Anything created after the era when people thought powdered wigs and carrier pigeons were high-tech.

examples.text: Modern democracies often use a federal system to manage large populations.
My grandma thinks using a microwave is 'modern magic' that might explode at any second.

words.meaning: Systems where people choose their leaders by voting.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To highlight that many modern free nations use various forms of federal systems.
hard.simple_explanation: Countries where the government is elected by the people.
hard.funny_explanation: Places where the citizens are the 'boss' and the politicians have to pass a job interview (called an election) every few years.

examples.text: Many modern democracies have adopted a federal structure to manage large populations.
In true democracies, even the cat would have a vote on which brand of tuna the family buys!

hard.real_world_analogy: A club where every member gets to vote on what games to play, instead of one kid deciding for everyone.

words.meaning: To give special attention to one specific thing.
In a way that is usual or happens often.
To call something by a specific name or term.

medium.simple_explanation: Mentioned or called something by a specific name or term.
medium.funny_explanation: How you are 'referred' to as 'The GOAT' by your friends after you finally land a bottle flip.

examples.text: This system of shared power is often referred to as federalism.
I like to be referred to as 'Captain Awesome,' but my teacher just calls me 'Late Again'.

words.meaning: Saying what someone or something is like.

medium.simple_explanation: Giving a detailed account or picture of something using words.
medium.funny_explanation: The impossible task of describing the color 'blurple' to someone who hasn't seen it.

examples.text: The author is describing how different levels of government work together.
Describing the smell of my gym bag would require words that haven't been invented yet.

words.meaning: Basic information without looking at small details.

medium.simple_explanation: Covering the main points without getting into small, specific details.
medium.funny_explanation: When your mom asks how school was and you say 'fine' to avoid explaining the cafeteria food fight.

examples.text: In a general sense, federalism means sharing power across the country.
I have a general idea of how to swim, which mostly involves splashing and yelling for help.

words.meaning: Words or expressions used in a specific subject.
The part of something that is left over.
Attempting to do or achieve something.
To know the meaning or purpose of something clearly.
A set of ideas that explain how something works.

medium.simple_explanation: An idea or system of rules intended to explain how something works.
medium.funny_explanation: My personal theory is that the TV remote has legs and hides specifically when my favorite show starts.

examples.text: The theory of federalism helps us understand why states have their own laws.
In theory, I should be done with my homework in ten minutes, but in reality, I'm watching cat videos.

words.meaning: How something is actually done in real life.

medium.simple_explanation: The actual application or use of an idea, rather than just the theory.
medium.funny_explanation: The scary moment when you actually have to use the math you learned instead of just staring at the chalkboard.

examples.text: The practice of federalism in India involves many local and state leaders.
Putting my 'calmness' into practice is hard when someone eats the last cookie.

words.meaning: A conversation or debate about a specific topic.

medium.simple_explanation: A conversation or debate about a particular topic to reach a decision or exchange ideas.
medium.funny_explanation: What your parents call it when they are actually just telling you why you're grounded.

examples.text: The class had a long discussion about whether the new law was fair.
Our discussion about which superhero is the best ended in a three-hour argument.

words.meaning: Relating to a system of central and state governments.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used as an adjective to describe the specific type of government or system being discussed.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to a system of government where several states form a unity but remain independent in internal affairs.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Team Captain' level of government that handles the big stuff like the army while the 'Players' (States) handle their own shoes.

examples.text: The federal government is responsible for the defense of the entire nation.
The federal rule says we must use the same money, but my mom says the rule in this house is 'clean your room!'

hard.real_world_analogy: A national sports league office that makes rules for all the different teams in the country.

words.meaning: Based on the set of laws governing a country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To emphasize that the rules of federalism are written in the nation's supreme law book.
hard.simple_explanation: Something that follows the rules set out in a country's Constitution.
hard.funny_explanation: The ultimate 'Teacher’s Manual' for a country. If a law doesn't follow this book, it gets a big red 'X' and is thrown out!

examples.text: The Supreme Court protects the constitutional rights of every citizen.
My constitutional right to eat cookies was sadly overruled by my mom's 'broccoli policy'.

hard.real_world_analogy: The official Rulebook of Cricket that every player and umpire must follow, no matter what.

words.meaning: Legal rules or conditions within a document.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the specific clauses or laws mentioned in the Constitution that allow federalism to work.
hard.simple_explanation: Specific requirements or legal conditions within a document.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Fine Print' in a contract. It's the part that says exactly who gets to do what, like who gets the TV remote on Saturdays.

examples.text: The Constitution has clear provisions regarding the distribution of taxes.
There are no provisions in our house rules for 'Infinite Bedtime,' much to my disappointment.

hard.real_world_analogy: The specific list of 'Dos and Don'ts' written on the back of your school ID card.

words.meaning: Coming after something else in a sequence.
A detailed study to understand how something works.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text encourages students to look deeply at how policies affect the government's success.
hard.simple_explanation: A detailed examination of the elements or structure of something.
hard.funny_explanation: Being a 'Science Detective.' You take a topic apart like a clock to see what makes it tick (and hope you can put it back together).

examples.text: A careful analysis of the data showed that the new law was working well.
My analysis of the cookie jar proves that my brother was here, because there are crumbs everywhere!

hard.real_world_analogy: Breaking down a Lego castle to see exactly which bricks make the secret door slide open.

words.meaning: Sets of plans or rules used by governments.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the plans and actions taken by political parties and governments.
hard.simple_explanation: A set of ideas or plans that is used as a basis for making decisions.
hard.funny_explanation: A 'Game Plan' for the country. It's the government saying, 'This is how we're going to fix the roads and make sure everyone has internet.'

examples.text: The government introduced new policies to improve school education.
Our family policy is that whoever cooks the dinner doesn't have to wash the dishes!

hard.real_world_analogy: A basketball coach's strategy for how to defend and when to shoot.

words.meaning: Activities related to power and running a country.

medium.simple_explanation: The activities and power struggles involved in running a government or a country.
medium.funny_explanation: Basically a very complicated game of 'King of the Hill' played by adults in expensive suits.

examples.text: Understanding politics helps you see how laws are made and who makes them.
Cafeteria politics are intense; one wrong move and you're sitting by the trash can.

words.meaning: To make something more powerful or effective.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes how political practices have made the federal system more robust over time.
hard.simple_explanation: To have been made stronger or more powerful.
hard.funny_explanation: Like the government went to the gym for fifty years and now has huge 'Power Muscles' to handle big problems.

examples.text: Democracy in India has been strengthened by the active participation of its citizens.
I strengthened my cardboard fort by adding three rolls of duct tape!

hard.real_world_analogy: Adding extra pillars to a bridge so it can carry heavy trucks without shaking.

words.meaning: In the direction of something or someone.
The final part of a period or book.
To move focus or attention to a different topic.
Relating to a small town or nearby area.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to a nearby area, neighborhood, or city rather than the whole country.
medium.funny_explanation: The shops you can walk to in your mismatched socks without anyone caring.

examples.text: Local governments handle things like fixing streetlights and cleaning parks.
The local squirrels have a meeting on my roof every morning at 5 AM.

words.meaning: Something that has recently been created or started.
The number three in a series or sequence.
One of several levels in a layered system.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe the different levels (Central, State, and Local) of the Indian government.
hard.simple_explanation: One of several levels in an organization or system.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a bunk bed for the government. The top bunk is the Center, the middle bunk is the State, and the bottom bunk is the Local town.

examples.text: The third tier of government in India is the Panchayati Raj.
My birthday cake had three tiers, but I only wanted to eat the chocolatey top level!

hard.real_world_analogy: The different floors of a department store: clothes on the first floor, toys on the second, and food on the third.

words.meaning: To return to a topic mentioned before.
A clear difference between two things.

medium.simple_explanation: A striking difference between two things being compared.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like comparing a super-hero who is always early to a villain who is always late; you really notice how different they are!

examples.text: The contrast between the hot summer and cold winter was huge.
There is a massive contrast between my cat’s 'I’m starving' face and her 'I just ate your sandwich' face.

words.meaning: To remember something from the past.
Making something different than it was.
The main set of rules for a country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author introduces this to explain the fundamental set of rules that governs how a country like Belgium or Sri Lanka is run.
hard.simple_explanation: A set of basic laws and principles that a country is governed by.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate 'Ultimate Rulebook' for a country. It's like the instruction manual for a giant LEGO set, telling everyone which pieces go where and who is in charge of the bricks.

examples.text: The Constitution of India ensures that every citizen has the right to equality.
If our house had a constitution, the first rule would definitely be: 'No eating the last slice of pizza without a vote!'

hard.real_world_analogy: A constitution is like the 'Rulebook' of a board game that everyone must follow so the game stays fair and organized.

words.meaning: To make something smaller or less.
The main part that controls other parts.

medium.simple_explanation: The main or middle part of something that has the most power.
medium.funny_explanation: Think of the Central Government as the 'Headquarters' or the 'Brain' that tries to tell the arms and legs what to do.

examples.text: The central office makes the big decisions for all the branches.
My stomach is the central command for all my snack-related decisions.

words.meaning: Related to a specific area of a country.

medium.simple_explanation: Related to a specific area or part of a country.
medium.funny_explanation: If the whole country is a giant pizza, the regional parts are just the individual slices that might have different toppings.

examples.text: The regional government looks after the needs of the local people.
Our regional dialect means we say 'pop' while others say 'soda' or 'fizzy drink'.

words.meaning: Was present or real in a place.
Happening at a time before now.
The specific jobs or duties someone has.
To take something back or away.

medium.simple_explanation: To take something back or remove it.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when your mom gives you a cookie but then sees you haven't done your chores and 'withdraws' it from your hand.

examples.text: The offer was withdrawn because the company changed its mind.
I quickly withdrew my hand from the jar when I realized it was full of spiders, not candy.

words.meaning: Allowed or protected by the main laws.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the formal legal powers given to regional governments that are protected by the country's main laws.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to or permitted by the constitution of a country.
hard.funny_explanation: This is the 'Official Stamp of Approval.' If something is constitutional, it means the Big Boss Rulebook says, 'Yes, you are allowed to do this!'

examples.text: The regional governments were finally given constitutional powers that the center could not take away.
My dog thinks having three naps a day is his constitutional right as a citizen of this living room.

hard.real_world_analogy: It is like a 'VIP Pass' that is written into the party rules; nobody can kick you out of the party because the rules specifically say you belong there.

words.meaning: Needing someone else for help or support.

medium.simple_explanation: Needing someone or something else for support or to work correctly.
medium.funny_explanation: I am totally dependent on my alarm clock, but I still treat it like my worst enemy every morning.

examples.text: The success of the play is dependent on how well the actors practice.
My phone is dependent on its charger, and I am dependent on my phone for memes.

words.meaning: Changed from one way to another.

medium.simple_explanation: Moved or changed from one position or state to another.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you’re sitting in class and you shift your weight so the teacher thinks you’re paying attention but you're actually napping.

examples.text: The country shifted its focus to improving schools.
The blame shifted from the dog to the cat as soon as the cat knocked over the vase.

words.meaning: System where one central group holds power.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to contrast a system where one single central power holds all the cards, unlike a federal system.
hard.simple_explanation: A system of government where the central government holds all or most of the power.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a TV remote that only one person is allowed to hold. That person chooses the show, the volume, and even when the TV is turned off. That's a unitary system—one remote, one boss.

examples.text: Sri Lanka followed a unitary system where the national government held all authority.
In a unitary household, Mom decides what everyone eats for dinner, what time everyone sleeps, and even what socks you wear!

hard.real_world_analogy: A unitary system is like a single giant classroom where only the principal makes every single rule for every student directly.

words.meaning: Power shared between center and states.

medium.simple_explanation: A system where power is shared between a central government and smaller states.
medium.funny_explanation: It’s like a group project where the teacher (Central) handles the grading, but each student (State) gets to choose their own markers and glitter.

examples.text: A federal system prevents one person from having all the power.
In a federal household, Dad might control the budget, but I have federal power over my bedroom mess.

words.meaning: A specific type or style of something.
Related to real situations rather than ideas.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to what is actually done or used rather than just ideas.
medium.funny_explanation: Reading a book about biking is an idea; actually not falling into a bush is the practical part.

examples.text: For all practical purposes, the old car was impossible to fix.
A chocolate teapot is beautiful, but it has zero practical use.

words.meaning: The reasons why something is done.
Related to the whole country.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to a whole country rather than just a small part of it.
medium.funny_explanation: A national anthem is the song everyone has to stand up for, even if they can't hit the high notes.

examples.text: The national government handles issues that affect every citizen.
My national holiday plan involves sleeping for 24 hours straight.

words.meaning: People who guide or control a group.
Governing by dividing power between levels.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This is the core concept of the chapter, explaining how power is shared between the center and the states.
hard.simple_explanation: A system of government where power is shared between a central authority and smaller regional units.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like a 'Group Project' where the teacher handles the big stuff, but each student gets to decide how to decorate their own part of the poster. Everyone shares the work and the glory!

examples.text: Federalism allows both the central and state governments to work independently in their own areas.
If my siblings and I practiced federalism, I would control my room, they would control theirs, and Mom would only control the hallway!

hard.real_world_analogy: It's like a franchise business (like McDonald's); the main company sets the big rules, but the local owner decides who to hire and how clean to keep their specific shop.

words.meaning: A way of organizing or doing things.

medium.simple_explanation: A set of things or parts forming a whole or working together.
medium.funny_explanation: Your digestive system is the team that turns pizza into energy (and bathroom trips).

examples.text: The school has a new system for checking attendance.
My 'organization system' is just throwing everything into a pile and hoping for the best.

words.meaning: Split into different parts or groups.
The power to make decisions and orders.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To define the 'Central Authority'—the person or group that has the right to give orders and make decisions.
hard.simple_explanation: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.
hard.funny_explanation: The person with authority is the one who holds the megaphone. When they speak, everyone else has to at least pretend they are listening!

examples.text: The central authority is responsible for national defense and currency.
My cat has zero respect for my authority, especially when I tell him to get off the kitchen counter.

hard.real_world_analogy: An authority figure is like a referee in a football game; they have the power to blow the whistle and stop the play.

words.meaning: Many different types of things.
Smaller parts that make up a whole.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the smaller parts (like states or provinces) that make up the whole country.
hard.simple_explanation: Being a part of a whole; the individual units that make up a system.
hard.funny_explanation: Constituent units are like the ingredients in a sandwich. You have the bread, the cheese, and the lettuce. Each is a constituent part that makes the 'Whole Sandwich' delicious.

examples.text: India is made up of many constituent units called States and Union Territories.
The chocolate chips are the most important constituent units of a chocolate chip cookie.

hard.real_world_analogy: A constituent unit is like a single piece of a jigsaw puzzle. By itself it's just a shape, but together they form the full picture.

words.meaning: Single parts belonging to a larger group.
Group of states under one central government.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To label the actual group of states that have joined together under a central government.
hard.simple_explanation: An organization or country formed by a group of states that have joined together.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of a federation like 'The Avengers.' Every hero has their own super-powers, but they join together as a federation to save the world from the big bad guys.

examples.text: A federation usually has two levels of government—national and state.
The Federation of Bored Students decided to declare Friday as Official Nap Day.

hard.real_world_analogy: A federation is like a sports league (like the IPL) where different teams (states) follow the same league rules but run their own team affairs.

words.meaning: Different layers of power or organization.
All of something; the whole amount.
Having the duty to look after something.

medium.simple_explanation: Being the person who must take care of something or take the blame.
medium.funny_explanation: Being responsible means you’re the one everyone looks at when the goldfish starts floating sideways.

examples.text: The central government is responsible for the country's defense.
I am responsible for eating all the cookies, though I blame the ghost.

words.meaning: Specific areas of work or duty.

medium.simple_explanation: Topics or areas of activity that a government deals with.
medium.funny_explanation: In government, 'subjects' aren't just boring classes like Math; they are the big things like 'Who pays for the roads?'

examples.text: Defense and finance are subjects handled by the national government.
If 'Napping' were one of the subjects of government, I would be the President.

words.meaning: Shared by many people or groups.

medium.simple_explanation: Shared by or belonging to two or more people or groups.
medium.funny_explanation: Having a 'common' interest means you both like the same thing—like how everyone has a common interest in Friday afternoons.

examples.text: The two countries worked together for their common goal of peace.
The only thing my brother and I have in common is our DNA and our love for annoying each other.

words.meaning: Something that is helpful or important.

medium.simple_explanation: Something that is important or beneficial to a person or group.
medium.funny_explanation: It’s in your 'best interest' to eat your vegetables, but it’s in your 'fun interest' to eat cake.

examples.text: The law was passed in the interest of public safety.
My cat has no interest in my feelings, only in the sound of a can opening.

words.meaning: Large regions a country is divided into.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the administrative divisions of a country, similar to states in India.
hard.simple_explanation: Principal administrative divisions of a country or empire.
hard.funny_explanation: If a country was a giant pizza, the provinces would be the individual slices. Some might have more pepperoni, some might have extra cheese, but they are all part of the same pizza.

examples.text: Canada is divided into several provinces, each with its own local government.
I have declared my bedroom and the playroom as independent provinces of 'Me-Land'.

hard.real_world_analogy: Provinces are like the different departments in a supermarket—Produce, Bakery, and Dairy—all in one building but managing different things.

words.meaning: Areas that have their own local government.
Managing and running a place or organization.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain the act of managing or running the day-to-day affairs of a state.
hard.simple_explanation: Managing or running the operations and affairs of an organization or state.
hard.funny_explanation: This is the 'Busy Work.' It’s making sure the trash is picked up, the lights stay on, and nobody is driving on the wrong side of the road. It’s like being the captain of a ship making sure everything is ship-shape.

examples.text: State governments are responsible for administering laws related to education and health.
Administering my daily schedule is impossible when there are so many cartoons to watch!

hard.real_world_analogy: Administering is like being the stage manager of a play; you aren't the actor, but you make sure the props are ready and the curtains open on time.

words.meaning: To have and use a specific power.
Free from the control of others.

medium.simple_explanation: Not influenced or controlled by others; free.
medium.funny_explanation: Being independent is like finally getting your own room and realizing you have to clean it yourself.

examples.text: The two levels of government act independent of each other.
I’m an independent person, right up until I see a huge spider and call for help.

words.meaning: Not understanding something clearly.
The earth and all its people.
Nations with their own land and laws.

medium.simple_explanation: Large areas of land that have their own governments.
medium.funny_explanation: Earth is basically a giant apartment building, and countries are the separate apartments where everyone has their own rules.

examples.text: Many countries around the world use a federal system.
I want to visit all the countries where they serve chocolate for breakfast.

words.meaning: Related to how a country is governed.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To define the type of system (political) that countries use to organize their government and power.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to the government or the public affairs of a country.
hard.funny_explanation: Anything political is about 'Who gets to decide what.' It’s the art of arguing, voting, and choosing leaders without (hopefully) throwing any food.

examples.text: Only a few countries in the world have federal political systems.
Choosing the class monitor became a very intense political battle involving promises of free pencils.

hard.real_world_analogy: Political matters are like a family meeting where everyone debates where to go for summer vacation.

words.meaning: Sets of rules for doing things.

medium.simple_explanation: Different organized ways or methods of doing things.
medium.funny_explanation: Some computer systems work great, while others seem to have a 'system' for crashing at the worst possible time.

examples.text: Different countries have different political systems.
I have multiple systems for finding my socks, but none of them actually work.

words.meaning: People who belong to a particular country.

medium.simple_explanation: People who legally belong to a country and have rights there.
medium.funny_explanation: Citizens are the 'members' of the Country Club who have to follow the rules but also get to vote on the snacks.

examples.text: Citizens have the right to vote in a democracy.
As a citizen of this house, I demand more screen time and less broccoli.

words.meaning: Total number of people living somewhere.

medium.simple_explanation: The total number of people living in a particular area.
medium.funny_explanation: The population of my bedroom increases by 100% when my five annoying cousins come over for the weekend.

examples.text: The population of the city has grown rapidly over the years.
The ant population in my kitchen is currently outvoting me on who owns the sugar bowl.

words.meaning: Big in size, amount, or number.
To see or become aware of something.
Something that does not follow the rule.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To point out a case that does not follow the general rule (e.g., a large country that is not a federation).
hard.simple_explanation: A person or thing that is excluded from a general statement or does not follow a rule.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s the 'But, wait!' moment. If every bird flies, the Ostrich is the exception because it prefers to run like a racecar instead.

examples.text: While most large countries are federations, China is a major exception.
Everyone in my class likes chocolate, with the weird exception of Tim, who prefers plain crackers.

hard.real_world_analogy: An exception is like a 'Holiday' in a school week—it’s the one day that doesn’t follow the usual 'wake up early' rule.

words.meaning: A statement about what is allowed.
A drawing of the earth's surface.
Where information or something comes from.
A small book giving useful facts.
Business that prints and publishes books.

medium.simple_explanation: A company that prints and publishes books or newspapers.
medium.funny_explanation: It's not a machine that squishes things; it's a place where they turn messy ideas into neat, printed books.

examples.text: The university press published a new book on history.
If I had my own press, I’d print a book called '101 Ways to Get Out of Doing Homework'.

words.meaning: The area where someone has legal power.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this term to define the specific legal boundaries and authorities of different levels of government.
hard.simple_explanation: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments over a specific area or subject.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of it as your 'Legal Bubble'. If your mom has jurisdiction over the kitchen, you can't decide to turn the oven into a volcano experiment without her okay!

examples.text: The local police do not have jurisdiction outside the city limits.
My cat thinks he has jurisdiction over the entire sofa, especially when I want to sit there.

hard.real_world_analogy: A school principal has jurisdiction over the students in their school, but they can't give detention to kids in the school down the street.

words.meaning: Related to the law.
The power to give orders or make decisions.

medium.simple_explanation: The power or right to give orders and make decisions.

hard.real_world_analogy: A VIP lounge where only people with a special golden ticket are allowed to enter.

words.meaning: The area where a government has power.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To define the legal area or range over which a government has authority.
hard.simple_explanation: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Zone of Control.' If a crime happens in one city, the police from another city can't usually come in and start bossing people around—it's out of their zone!

examples.text: The Supreme Court has jurisdiction over disputes between states.
You have no jurisdiction in this bedroom! Get out!

hard.real_world_analogy: A referee in a basketball game who has no power to blow the whistle during a nearby football match.

words.meaning: Belonging separately to each person or thing.

medium.simple_explanation: Belonging separately to each person or thing that has been mentioned.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when a teacher says 'Go to your respective seats' instead of everyone sitting in one giant, messy pile.

examples.text: The Union and State governments have jurisdiction over their respective subjects.
After the party, all the kids went back to their respective homes to sleep.

words.meaning: A land with its own people and government.
Separated into different parts or sections.
Moving to a position inside something.
Large parts that a country is split into.

medium.simple_explanation: The different regions or parts that a country is divided into.
medium.funny_explanation: The different 'neighborhoods' of a country, each with its own vibe and slightly different local rules.

examples.text: Sri Lanka is divided into provinces, but it doesn't function like a federation.
In my imaginary kingdom, I would divide the land into 'Chocolate Province' and 'Pizza Province'.

words.meaning: Continuing for more time than before.
The past form of the word be.
Passed power down to a lower level.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to explain how power is passed down from higher levels (State) to lower levels (Local bodies).
hard.simple_explanation: Transferred or passed down (power or responsibility) to a lower level.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a teacher getting tired of picking the lunch menu and letting the students choose instead—giving away the power!

examples.text: In 1992, more powers were devolved to the local panchayats in India.
Mom devolved the responsibility of washing the dog to me, and now I'm soaked.

hard.real_world_analogy: A CEO of a big company letting the branch managers decide what color to paint their own offices.

words.meaning: Organized groups with a specific purpose.
Something that is right and has no mistakes.
